newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere drops on Thomson worries.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere drops on Thomson worries.

text.p: Shares in France's Lagardere Groupe fell by 4.5 percent on Monday morning on investor worries about a political backlash against the planned sale of Thomson Multimedia to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.

French opposition parties, labour unions and a majority in an opinion poll are increasingly voicing resistance to recent government plans for privatisations of French companies such as GAN-CIC, CCF, Thomson SA, Credit Lyonnais and Air France.
"Lagardere is down because of the recent news articles that put in doubt the Thomson deal," a dealer said.
On Wednesday October 16, the French government announced it had selected Lagardere Groupe over Alcatel Alsthom to buy loss-making Thomson after a 14 billion franc capital injection.
Under the Lagardere deal, Thomson's 100-percent television and videorecorder maker Thomson Multimedia will be sold to Daewoo Electronics, also for one franc.

A survey of 1,004 voters released on Sunday by the business daily La Tribune Desfosses said 72 percent disapproved of the sale for the symbolic price to the Lagardere conglomerate because it did not reflect the group's value.
Twelve percent said the sale was right because of the group's heavy debts.

Loser Alcatel Alsthom said in a statememt on Friday that its offer foresaw it would have taken 100 percent of Thomson Multimedia. It said it would have looked for an Asian partner, in order to be able to sell better on the southeast Asian market.
"This new group would have formed the basis of a global industrial project in which the French interests would have been firmly represented," Alcatel said.
"The benefits for French industry would have been important, was it not for the synergies with the digital network activities Alcatel Alsthom," it added.
The Les Echos newspaper said, in an unsourced report, that Alcatel would have transferred to the state any capital gain it would make on the eventual sale of part of Thomson Multimedia.
France's Privatisation Commission and the European Commission still had to approve the deal.
